2 5. The facts may be recounted in brief.

6. The State of Haryana issued a Notification under Section 4 of the Act on 25.09.1979, proposing to acquire 39 acres, 3 kanals and 15 marlas land, situated in Village Bawal, Tehsil Bawal,
District Mohindergarh, for the purpose of construction of a New Grain Market, and Link Road Dharuhera-Shahjahanpur Road leading to the Grain Market itself.
The New Grain Market and the Link Road were to be constructed by the Market Committee, Rewari, which is the appellant herein.
7. A Notification under Section 6 of the Act was issued on 15.07.1981 for the land admeasuring 39 acres, 3 kanals and 13 marlas.
The Land Acquisition Collector, by an Award dated 11.04.1986, awarded compensation at the rate of Rs. 16,000/- per acre.

The landowners, being dissatisfied, filed references under Section 18 of the Act, which were allowed in part vide an Award dated 30.08.1990 when the Reference Court fixed the compensation at the rate of Rs. 50,000/- per acre.
The claimant  landowners were also held entitled to solatium at the rate of 30%, an additional Market Committee, Rewari vs Nemi Chand (D) Thr.

8. The landowners were still dissatisfied with the compensation, and proceeded to file Regular First Appeals before the High Court.
It appears that the appellant - Committee was also aggrieved by the rate of compensation determined by the Reference Court, hence it also filed Cross Objections.
9. The High Court allowed a bunch of appeals vide a common judgment dated 12.11.2009 and enhanced the market value of the  3 acquired land to Rs.3,84,000/- per acre.

. The Judgement dated 12.11.2009 of the learned Single Judge of the High Court had been followed by the coordinate Benches of the High Court, granting the same rate of compensation in other first appeals, arising out of the same acquisition, vide one of the impugned judgements dated 05.07.2010.
11. The Market Committee, Rewari being aggrieved by the enhanced rate of compensation, has preferred these appeals.

12. We have heard Mr. Hemant Gupta, learned Additional Advocate General appearing on behalf of the appellant - Committee as well as Mr. Shish Pal Laler, learned counsel appearing on behalf of the  4 respondent - landowners and carefully perused the material placed on record.
13. Two primary contentions have been raised by Mr. Hemant Gupta, learned Additional Advocate General for the appellant.
He submits that   i) The sale transaction of small pieces of land are  absolutely irrelevant and could not be relied upon for  determining the market value of the acquired land.

Reliance is placed upon Tarlochan Singh & Anr. vs. State  of Punjab & Ors., (1995) 2 SCC 424 and Union of India &
 Anr. vs. Ram Phool & Anr., (2003) 10 SCC 167.
 ii) Alternatively, the High Court ought to have imposed  deduction of more than 60% on the sale consideration  reflected in Sale Deeds (Exhibit P-1 and Exhibit P-6).
14.

4 this Court in a catena of decisions has held that parallels with small pieces of land need not be outrightly rejected when assessing the value of larger parcels of land, if the Court finds that the former have a bearing on determination of the market value of the acquired land.
If the Sale Deeds can assist the Court in completing an accurate estimation of the fair and just price of the acquired land, these smaller pieces of land may also be used as analogies.
He further submits that the High Court has already imposed a cut of 60% which is on the higher side.

15. Having evaluated the rival submissions made on behalf of both sides, we are of the view that there is no hard and fast rule  5 that sales of small pieces of land, which are otherwise relevant,
are liable to be rejected only on the premise that the acquired land in question is much larger.
It will all depend upon the facts and circumstances of each case to determine the relevance of sales of smaller pieces of land.
16. In the case at hand, about 40 acres land was acquired for the purpose of construction of New Grain Market and for construction of the link road.

It has been found, as a matter of fact, that the acquired land was located in a semi-urban area and was surrounded by schools, markets, educational institutions, and had the potentiality to be used for residential and commercial purposes.
The acquired land is apparently abutting the road.
The Sale Deeds (Exhibit P-1 and P-6) are of land in the adjoining area which was purportedly sold for commercial purposes.
Both the Sale Deeds were executed much before Section 4 Notification was issued Market Committee, Rewari vs Nemi Chand (D) Thr.

5 on 25.09.1979.
There were other sale deeds relied upon by the owners like Exhibit P-2 and Exhibit P-5 but these have been rejected by the High Court, and rightly so, being post the Section 4 Notification.

17. Since the acquired land is a composite chunk of around 40 acres, the High Court deemed it appropriate to apply a cut of 60%
on the sale consideration depicted in the sales cited before it (Exhibit P-1 and Exhibit P-6).
No other sales of land having a bearing on the assessment of the market value of the acquired land has been brought on record from the side of the State or the land owners.
Hence, we are satisfied that the High Court rightly relied upon the Sale Deeds (Exhibit P-1 and P-6) in order to determine the  6 market value of the acquired land.
We do not find any error of law or fact committed by the High Court in placing reliance on Exhibit P-1 and Exhibit P-6 for the purpose of assessing the market value of the acquired land.

The decisions of this Court relied upon by the learned Additional Advocate General, appearing on behalf of the appellant, are distinguishable on facts and the same cannot be held to have laid down a binding principle that the sales of small pieces of land cannot form basis for determining the market value of a much larger chunk of acquired land.
18. For the reasons aforesaid, we do not find any merit in these appeals, which are accordingly dismissed.
19. The interim orders passed by this court on 01.04.2011 and 16.10.2015 are hereby vacated.
